intro: Beneath the streets of İzmir lies its forerunner: Smyrna, an ancient city in İzmir province whose story runs from the 3rd millennium BC to today. It is famed above all for the Roman agora at the foot of Kadifekale, and that is where our walk begins.
history: In the 4th century BC a new chapter opened, when Alexander's general Lysimachus founded New Smyrna around Kadifekale. Then disaster struck: an earthquake in AD 178 destroyed the city. Yet Smyrna rose again, and its agora was rebuilt under Emperor Marcus Aurelius.
structure-1: You are now standing in the Roman Agora. In Roman times this square was the city's commercial and administrative centre. Imagine merchants and officials crossing paths right where you stand.
structure-3: Before you is the Gate of Faustina, the monumental gate in the agora of Smyrna. It was dedicated to Faustina, wife of Emperor Marcus Aurelius.
structure-4: Now look at the agora columns. These are the remains of the stoas and public buildings that once surrounded the square. Let your imagination fill in the buildings around them.
structure-5: And finally, Kadifekale: the acropolis of ancient Smyrna, set atop the hill that overlooks İzmir. The old city and the new still share this view.
highlights: As you wander through the agora, don't miss the Basilica, and take your time there.
facts: Did you know? Smyrna was one of the Seven Churches of Revelation, and one that has survived to the present day. It was also one of seven cities claiming to be Homer's birthplace, and the one with the strongest claim. After the earthquake of AD 178, the agora's three-storey basilica was rebuilt with a donation from the empress Faustina. And in the fourth century BC the city moved, on Alexander's orders, to the slopes of today's Kadifekale; İzmir still sits on that plan.
outro: This brings our tour of Smyrna to an end. Before you leave, please keep the stones untouched, stay on the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking these ancient streets with us, and enjoy your visit.
